Remarkably, Deep CNN (DCNNs) have demonstrated outstanding classification capabilities in the diagnosis of MI, leading to their increasing prominence in recent times.

articleTitle: A Review on Privacy and Anonymity in Blockchain Security
publicationTitle: 2023 Eleventh International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Information Systems (ICICIS)
abstract: The advent of blockchain technology has revolutionized various industries, including finance, supply chain management, and healthcare. However, concerns regarding privacy and anonymity in blockchain security have emerged as significant challenges. This paper aims to investigate the current state of privacy and anonymity in blockchain security by gathering insights from a diverse group of recent research. we explore the current understanding, practices, and challenges related to privacy and anonymity in blockchain security, to identify the importance of them, assess the effectiveness of existing privacy-enhancing techniques, and uncover potential areas for improvement.

articleTitle: Towards Universal Metrics for Hardware Cybersecurity Assessment
publicationTitle: 2023 Eleventh International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Information Systems (ICICIS)
abstract: The number of computers has soared around the globe, notably with the omnipresence of the Internet of Things (IoT). Cybersecurity threats have naturally become a major concern. When mentioning cybersecurity, software and networking aspects often come first to mind. Nevertheless, hardware attacks are being carried out and should not be neglected. Metrics are a powerful indicator tool for better management of systems, software and devices. They allow objective assessment of the cybersecurity of a computer system. The scientific literature review showed scarcity in discussing hardware metrics from a cybersecurity aspect. This paper presents metrics to evaluate the security of a device against hardware attacks without the need of testing the attack on the device (i.e. pen-test the device). This is done by assessing the characteristics and the mitigation the device has. A tool to automate some of the cybersecurity metrics proposed has also been implemented as a proof of concept and is also presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Hyperparameter-optimized CNN and CNN-LSTM for Predicting the Remaining Useful Life of Lithium-Ion Batteries
publicationTitle: 2023 Eleventh International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Information Systems (ICICIS)
abstract: This paper introduces novel advancements in predicting the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of Lithium-Ion Batteries (LIBs) using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Convolutional Neural Network-Long Short-Term Memory (CNN-LSTM) models, fine-tuned with Bayesian Optimization. Our study presents three key novelties. First, the research is rooted in the utilization of a publicly available dataset comprising 124 LIB cells, ensuring enhanced model generalization, and capturing a diverse array of battery usage patterns. Second, Bayesian Optimization is employed to optimize the hyperparameters of both models, leading to enhanced predictive accuracy. Third, we perform a rigorous direct comparison between the CNN and CNN-LSTM models, demonstrating the superiority of the CNN-LSTM model in RUL prediction by approximately 0.89%. Additionally, this study sheds light on the interpretability of the CNN-LSTM model, providing valuable insights into factors influencing RUL estimation. Both models exhibit high precision, with Mean Absolute Error (MAE) values of 85.6365 and 84.8746 cycles, respectively. The outcomes underscore the practical significance of accurate RUL prediction in LIBs, benefiting Electric Vehicles, battery manufacturing, and efficient maintenance planning. Our research contributes to advancing RUL prediction for LIBs in electric vehicles and energy storage systems.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Ensemble Deep Learning Algorithms for Prediction of Pandemic Disease
publicationTitle: 2023 Eleventh International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Information Systems (ICICIS)
abstract: To ensure effective healthcare administration and preventive measures, it is crucial to timely monitor and forecast the occurrence of severe diseases prior to their escalation into a pandemic. This research focuses on the COVID-19 pandemic as a case study to examine the importance of understanding the prognosis of viral diseases. The profound COVID-19 menace has exerted a significant impact on the worldwide health security landscape, necessitating the development of state-of-the-art computer models to enhance surveillance, management, and mitigation strategies. In order to forecast the severity of a disease before it becomes a pandemic, the research aims to develop a complete model that assesses healthcare factors at both the individual and community levels. This study has carefully evaluated the outcomes of several experiments using the ensemble, ResNet, and DenseNet models using a variety of performance metrics in order to achieve this goal. The ensemble model continuously demonstrated outstanding performance on all metrics, with a f1-score of 97% and accuracy. The DenseNet model obtained a 93% accuracy and f1-score, while the ResNet model obtained an 89% accuracy and an 88% f1-score. The models showcased in this paper demonstrated exceptional precision and possess the capability to aid in forecasting COVID-19. The effectiveness of computer models in correctly forecasting the illness was assessed using chest x-ray images. This experiment allows us to acquire a thorough comprehension of the advantages and disadvantages of various computer models in forecasting severe illnesses. Acquiring this knowledge will facilitate the creation of prediction systems that are more precise and effective in diagnosing any medical condition. The resultant outcome highlights the efficiency of ensemble techniques in utilising the combined benefits of several models. The information that is gained from this research aims to go beyond theory and apply it to the real world of hospital administration.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Models for Skin Cancer Detection: A review
publicationTitle: 2023 Eleventh International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Information Systems (ICICIS)
abstract: Skin cancer is one of those most common cancers that affect people. Due to various factors, DNA mutations grow out of control and eventually lead to skin cancer. Early cancer detection can improve the likelihood of successful treatment. Applications for computer-aided diagnosis are now used in almost every industry, especially the health sector. The data of ill people is saved in computers to create biomedical datasets. It is crucial to find a reliable method for early skin cancer diagnosis and type classification. Computer- aided detection using Deep Learning (DL) and Machine Learning (ML) shows tremendous growth in the medical field. Medical images are considered as the actual origin of appropriate information required for diagnosis of disease. This paper presents a thorough and methodical analysis of deep learning methods for skin cancer early detection. On this subject, a great deal of research has been done. Thus, it's imperative to assess, classify, and integrate the results of previous research. In order to facilitate comprehension of research findings, they are presented using tables, methodologies, and frameworks.

articleTitle: A Smart and Eco-friendly Personal Heating and Cooling system
publicationTitle: 2023 Eleventh International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Information Systems (ICICIS)
abstract: Climate change has become ineluctable and has tremendous negative effects on the environment. Human thermal comfort has been an important survival matter for mankind since the dawn of humanity. Many heating and cooling devices have been developed but only a few are considered eco-friendly. This paper presents an ecological thermal regulatory portable prototype device named Thermo Pal, Thermo Pal is capable of heating and cooling. Thermo Pal consists of a small bag and a belt that can be attached to any body part. The device was found efficient, small-sized, light weighted, and consumed low power. It is able to provide 1 hour of cooling or 3 hours of heating. A novel conceptual smart automated model is also proposed.

articleTitle: ML Driven Priority-Based Constrained Routing for Pollution Management in ITS
publicationTitle: 2023 Eleventh International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Information Systems (ICICIS)
abstract: Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) seek to enhance traffic safety, mobility, and efficiency through advanced technologies. Priority assignment, a fundamental component of ITS, allocates priority to various types of vehicles or roads based on their significance and urgency. In this study, we explore the implementation of priority-based constrained routing for road vehicles in ITS, leveraging machine learning techniques and dynamic routing algorithms. Our objective is to enhance traffic management and efficiency by addressing the limitations of traditional routing methods that do not account for vehicle priorities. By employing machine learning models within a priority-based routing system, dynamic priorities can be accurately assigned to vehicles in real-time, facilitating more effective traffic management decisions. This approach mitigates congestion and reduces travel times for high-priority vehicles, presenting an innovative means of refining traffic control strategies. The findings hold substantial implications for real-world ITS systems, as they can alleviate traffic congestion, improve traffic flow, enhance efficiency, and manage pollution levels in specific areas.

articleTitle: Recognizing Hand Movements Using EEG-Signal Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 Eleventh International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Information Systems (ICICIS)
abstract: Classifying various precise manual movements based on electroencephalogram (EEG) signals presents an important research obstacle, particularly in the category of motor rehabilitation within brain-computer interface (BCI) applications. This study focuses on classifying EEG signals into six hand movement classes (forward, backward, up, down, right, left) utilizing machine learning and deep learning methods. The goal is to detect the person's current thoughts and intentions, including motor imagery and real movements, to assist individuals with physical disabilities or limb loss in controlling their robotic arms. After data collection and preprocessing, feature extraction is performed on the EEG signals obtained from the five signal bands (alpha, beta, theta, delta, gamma). Deep learning techniques include the use of recurrent neural networks with long short-term memory (RNN-LSTM) and convolutional neural networks (CNN), in addition to more traditional classifiers like Support Vector Machines (SVM) and Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA), an overall best accuracy 70% is achieved in detecting the 6 hand movements classes from one subject. DWT with Logistic Regression, also CSP using SVM (one vs rest) achieved the same accuracy. EEG-Net also got 70% accuracy on the 6 classes. 93% accuracy is achieved for binary classification (2 classes) with CSP as a feature and Random Forest classifier also DWT using LSTM achieved the same accuracy using a 60-channel EEG system, the results that overcome the results from literature review on the same dataset. Cross subjects' technique is experimented also in this study. Using cross subjects' data from 4 classes, CSP using LSTM shows high accuracy of 61%. The use of a 60-channel EEG system and the adoption of deep learning techniques resulted in the best accuracy for hand movement recognition in this study.

articleTitle: Advancing Egyptian Arabic Speech Emotion Recognition: Insights from 2D Representations and Model Evaluations
publicationTitle: 2023 Eleventh International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Information Systems (ICICIS)
abstract: This paper addresses the existing disparity in Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) advancements, where languages like English and German have made progress, while Arabic has received limited attention. The study aims to give real-time, effective techniques for identifying user emotions from speech, focusing on the widely spoken and comprehended Egyptian Arabic dialect. Human emotions play a crucial role in all of our interactions and relationships, determining expressions like happiness, despair, and grief. As technology integration grows, the ability of computers to perceive and comprehend human emotions becomes increasingly vital. Teaching computers emotional understanding enables personalized and adaptable systems. This study undertakes a comparative analysis of various audio image representations and classification models, utilizing EYASE [1] and EAED [20] datasets to identify the optimal ways to achieve this. After preprocessing the audios to eliminate noise, such as background music, the dataset undergoes augmentation to increase class samples. The Mel-frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs), Log-Mel spectrogram, discrete Meyer wavelet, and waveform audio features were used to represent each audio file. The models include a combination of VGG19 for features extraction & Support Vector Machine (SVM) for classification, ResNet50 with global average pooling and dense layer, and a custom Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). Notably, the CNN achieves the most promising outcomes, attaining accuracies of 90.1% for 3 emotion classes, 88.6% for 4 classes, and 76.3% for 5 classes through log-mel spectrograms.

articleTitle: Emotion Recognition: Enhancing Human-Computer Interaction
publicationTitle: 2023 Eleventh International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Information Systems (ICICIS)
abstract: In today's world, Human-Computer Interactions (HCI) aims to replicate genuine human-to-human communication, wherein emotions play a pivotal role. The human voice carries a rich array of emotions, making speech a natural and powerful means of communication. Emotions greatly influence human interactions, encompassing facial expressions, body gestures, voice characteristics, intonation, and linguistic contents. This study delves into how the choice of classification method, combined with the optimal features and data augmentation, impacts the accuracy of speech emotion detection. Careful selection of hand-crafted features combined with the classification model plays a crucial role in simplifying the computational complexity. Deep learning (DL) models have brought a paradigm shift in Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) by mimicking the brain's processes and improving classification accuracy. The developed classification model, which is a 1-Dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), surpasses conventional Machine Learning (ML) techniques regarding classification tasks. In contrast to previous research, which has focused on emotions within a single linguistic framework, this analysis encompasses a wide array of language datasets.

articleTitle: On Development of Computer Aided System for Detecting Brain Neurological Disorders
publicationTitle: 2023 Eleventh International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Information Systems (ICICIS)
abstract: Brain Neurological disorder is a serious disease that affects human's brain and may cause him to suffer. Computer Aided Systems have emerged in our daily life to provide support for the doctors and have become promising tools that assist healthcare professionals in predicting and diagnosing pathologies and recommend treatments for individual patients. This survey paper aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the current state of computer-aided systems for detecting brain neurological disorders including Alzheimer's disease and Autism spectrum disorders. The paper focuses on gathering the most popular datasets with different types such as EEG and fMRI that were utilized in the development and evaluation of these systems. We explored diverse range of features employed in these datasets which are vitally important for the precise identification and classification of brain neurological disorders. Additionally, recent studies in this field are collected and analyzed, with a particular emphasis on the methodologies utilized in the design and implementation of their models. These encompass traditional machine learning algorithms such as SVM, RF, DT and K-NN, as well as deep learning approaches, including CNN, DNN and Autoencoders. The findings are presented in a table format, showcasing the accuracy results of the different methodologies, sorted in descending order. Furthermore, the paper concludes by presenting insightful charts for statistical analysis that can guide researchers in understanding the current state of the art in this field to assist them in the development of more accurate, efficient, and accessible tools, utilizing the data accumulated throughout the survey paper, to enable early detection, diagnosis and ultimately improving patient outcomes and quality of life.

articleTitle: DeepFake Detection System using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 Eleventh International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Information Systems (ICICIS)
abstract: Due to the growing usage of DeepFake technology to produce fake photos and videos, the problem of DeepFake identification has become a serious concern in recent years. With the use of this technology, fake material that is difficult to tell apart from real content may be produced. Therefore, the development of accurate DeepFake detection algorithms is essential to identify and prevent the spread of manipulated content. However, current publicly available DeepFake detection datasets suffer from a lack of diversity, with only a few actors appearing in multiple videos. This results in an oversampled training dataset, leading to model overfitting and inadequate performance when tested on new data. The overfitting problem can cause deep neural networks to focus more on facial features than on specific traits of DeepFake content, thereby reducing the model's ability to generalize. To address this issue and broaden the training dataset's variety, we suggest applying data augmentation methods like Face Cutout and Random Erase. The Face Cutout technique randomly removes a rectangular area of an image containing the face, while the Random Erase technique randomly removes a rectangular area of the image. These techniques introduce variations in the images, making it more challenging for the model to overfit and focus on specific traits of DeepFake content. We evaluated our approach using several models and achieved significant accuracy improvements using the EfficientnetV2B0 model and Random Erase augmentation.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Centralized, Distributed and Federated Learning for IoT Intrusion Detection Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 Eleventh International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Information Systems (ICICIS)
abstract: Introducing smart intrusion detection systems (IDSs) in the IoT system was a crucial requirement in the last decades to secure these systems due to the high sensitivity of the sensed data. Smart IDS has often been built based on a machine/deep learning model trained at a centralized node in the cloud. However, the centralized learning approach violates data privacy since IoT nodes are required to share their data to the cloud to train the model. Distributed and federated learning approaches were introduced to solve this issue by keeping data within the local network and letting the edge devices train the model. In this paper, a comparative study among centralized, distributed, and federated learning approaches is presented. First, a deep learning model is proposed to identify traffic behavior using CICIDS2017 dataset. The three learning approaches are then applied with the proposed model to evaluate the effect of each approach on the model accuracy. In the centralized learning approach, an F-Score of 98% can be achieved. Moreover, the dataset is split over ten simulated nodes with various data distribution and entropies to evaluate the distributed and federated learning approaches. In distributed learning, the F-Score ranges between 63% to 93% with an average of 78% over the ten nodes. In the federated learning, the F-Score ranges between 73% to 98% with an average of 89% over the ten nodes. This result confirms that IDSs based on federated learning are a promising solution for both accuracy and preserving data privacy.

articleTitle: Time Stretching and Pitch Shifting for Anomalous Sound Detection in Fan Sound Signal using MobileNetV2
publicationTitle: 2023 Eleventh International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Information Systems (ICICIS)
abstract: Anomalous sound detection means the ability to identify between normal and anomalous sounds specifically within the context of sound produced by a fan machine. This capability is of vital importance to various industries as it enables the prediction of issues and alerts maintenance teams before significant damage occurs. This leads to cost reduction and efficient resource allocation, especially considering the wide range of applications involving fan machines. In this study, we provide an approach for the unsupervised learning-based anomalous sound detection (ASD) of fan sound using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). We used a MobileNetV2-based system established by the Detection and Classification of Acoustic Scenes and Events (DCASE) competition organizers as a starting point to implement this system. To make the system tailored more specifically toward fan sound signals, we have tried two distinct approaches. The first approach depended on applying transformations to the data using data augmentation after experimenting with several techniques we found that time stretch, along with pitch shift, yielded the most effective results. The second approach involved incorporating the Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) into our proposed system to enhance the accuracy of the detection. Using an exhaustive dataset that included normal and anomalous fan sound recordings, our proposed approaches were evaluated.

articleTitle: Deepfake Detection Using EfficientNet and XceptionNet
publicationTitle: 2023 Eleventh International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Information Systems (ICICIS)
abstract: The increasing prevalence of manipulated media, particularly deepfake videos, poses significant challenges in distinguishing real from fake content. This paper addresses the issue of detecting deepfake videos using advanced CNN architectures such as EfficientNet-B4 and XceptionNet. The FF++ and Celeb-DF (v2) datasets are used to compare real and fake videos. The methodology involves preprocessing the Celeb- DF dataset by extracting frames and isolating faces, training the models, and evaluating their performance using log loss and Area Under the Curve (AUC) metrics. The study shows that both models are effective in accurately classifying real and fake videos and highlights the importance of continuously updating deepfake detection algorithms in response to evolving deepfake generation techniques.

articleTitle: Backslash map: An Automated Vulnerability Scanner
publicationTitle: 2023 Eleventh International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Information Systems (ICICIS)
abstract: Web application vulnerability detection is critical to cybersecurity. Web applications are vulnerable to attacks from a variety of sources, with varying degrees of scale and complexity. Therefore, it becomes essential to employ an automated tool that can effectively examine and identify vulnerabilities within the application. This research paper introduces Backslash Map, an automated system for penetration testing that enables efficient identification of web application vulnerabilities. The proposed system utilizes signature-based scanning techniques and predefined payloads. It offers key features such as subdomain enumeration (passive or active), port scanning, and detection of SQL injection, server-side template injection, and code execution vulnerabilities. During the vulnerability assessment, Backslash Map inspects and filters requests to identify vulnerable endpoints while performing subdomain enumeration on domain services. The experimental results prove the promising performance of the proposed system when compared with the state-of-the-art.

articleTitle: Text-to-Image Synthesis using Generative Adversarial Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 Eleventh International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Information Systems (ICICIS)
abstract: Text-to-image synthesis is considered a unique problem in image synthesis, which is the task of generating image from input text. Previously, the purpose of text-to-image synthesiswas to match words and images using retrieval methods basedon a phrase or collection of keywords. With the evolution ofdeep learning, particularly the usage of generative models, image synthesis has made potentially significant advancements. One of the most significant generative models are Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), and they have been widely successfully utilized in various domains. In this study proposes our model, examines and summarizes recent work on GAN-based text-to-image synthesis, as well as providing an overview of the evolution of both classic and cutting-edge models. The usual structure of each category is described in depth. The survey presents a thorough review of the development of GAN-based text to image synthesis. Finally, Dynamic Memory GAN with Contrastive Learning (DMGAN+CL) with prompt engineering, which optimizes and acquires consistent textual representations for captions using the contrastive learning technique. We tested our technique on the CUB-200 dataset, and the findings demonstrate that our framework achieved comparable results with other typical GANs architectures in text-to-image synthesis.

articleTitle: Using NLP for Functional Size Measurement of IoT Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 Eleventh International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Information Systems (ICICIS)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) was born when embedded systems represented in edge devices were able to send and receive data back and forth via the Internet and process these data in real-time near the same physical environments they are deployed. Hence, enabling the existence of numerous smart applications and devices used in daily life. The ubiquity of IoT applications required means to measure software-provided functionality. Functional size measurement is a tool used for this purpose in addition to obtaining technical indicators early in the design phase. The Common Software Measurement International Consortium (COSMIC) method is an international standard for functional size measurement of a software. A study [?] has represented a tool to automatically retrieve source codes of IoT edge devices and measure their COSMIC functional size through analysing the code. Nevertheless, the tool was limited to certain Arduino libraries. In this paper, Natural language processing (NLP), a sub-field of Artificial intelligence that enables computers to process human language is integrated with the tool presented to analyse the source code. Hence, enabling the tool to measure the COSMIC functional size of any source code retrieved automatically. This paper presents an approach to modify the tool presented in [1] by using NLP to automatically analyse and measure the COSMIC functional size of source codes without being limited to a certain number of libraries.

articleTitle: Quantifying Real-time Pollution Impact of Vehicle Rerouting on Initial Pollution Levels
publicationTitle: 2023 Eleventh International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Information Systems (ICICIS)
abstract: Since the last century, the problem of air pollution started facing human beings as it started rising significantly. This proposed different health threats to humans, and it is affecting the environment harshly. Traffic and most transportation methods are a significant contributor to this increase in pollution levels due to burning fuels to keep these vehicles moving. Since people strongly depend on these vehicles for their everyday commute moving from starting points to destinations, it will help if the real time contribution this route on pollution levels can be predicted and how it will impact it. This study aims at finding the real- time emissions produced by travelling through a route with a specific vehicle based on studying different characteristics of this route and finding its impact on the initial pollution levels. It studies the effect locally within the edges (roads) taken through this route and regionally within the whole area covered by the network. Studying the impact of moving through a specific route on initial pollution levels is essential as with this information, people can take smarter decisions regarding the routes taken for their transportation from one place to another by choosing the route with the least fingerprint on the environment.

articleTitle: Traditional and Deep Learning Techniques in Image Steganography: Recent Advances
publicationTitle: 2023 Eleventh International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Information Systems (ICICIS)
abstract: For many decades however recently super increased; the importance of securing the private information of individuals or organizations. Therefore, numerous researchers are motivated to be involved in the challenge of building intelligent, flexible, secured, imperceptive, bumped bit embedding rates and robust models of Stenography. Image steganography is a way of concealing data, such as text, pictures, or videos, under an image that acts as a cover. Recent years have seen an increase in interest in deep learning technology, which has been proven to be a powerful mechanism in a number of uses, such as image steganography. This paper's primary goal is to investigate and clarify three main types of image steganography techniques: traditional, convolutional neural network-based, and generative adversarial network-based. An explanation of the datasets and evaluation measures is provided along with the approach. A comprehensive summary of various image steganography techniques is introduced. Finally, a discussion on the potential directions for this field's future is introduced.

articleTitle: Analysis of Deep Learning Models for Voice Pathology Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 Eleventh International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Information Systems (ICICIS)
abstract: Voice disorders affect a significant portion of the global population, particularly those in vocally demanding professions such as singers, actors, teachers, and lawyers. Early detection and diagnosis of voice pathology diseases are critical to improving treatment outcomes and preventing further damage to the vocal cords. Digital processing of speech signals has emerged as a promising technique for analyzing voice vibrations and identifying deformities in the vocal cord function. In this paper, a cost-effective computational method involves processing the voice signal by passing to a stack of band-pass filters, dividing the processed signal of each filter to a set of overlapped frames, applying the autocorrelation formula to every single frame, and using entropy to extract features. The method has shown promise in reliably detecting and classifying voice pathology diseases, but further research is required to confirm its efficacy and reliability. Deep learning algorithms and Mel spectrogram feature extraction techniques are present in this paper for voice pathology detection. VGG16, VGG19, and ResNet50 are compared. The system demonstrated high prediction accuracy results using ResNet50 on training and testing dataset. The system shows potential for clinical applications in voice disorder assessment and diagnosis. The system also holds promise as a telemedicine tool, enabling remote assessment and monitoring of patients' vocal health.

articleTitle: A Review on Cyber-Physical-Social Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 Eleventh International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Information Systems (ICICIS)
abstract: A cyber-physical-social system (CPSS) is a brand-new paradigm of cyber-physical and cyber-social systems that integrates dynamic stochastic hybrid systems including computation, communication, sensing and actuation, and social systems. It is highly homogeneous and distributed. Its application can be seen in a variety of areas, including smart homes, industrial producers, infrastructures, smart cities, pharmaceuticals, healthcare systems, and many others. It can offer a greater degree of control and accessibility, as well as simplify and speed up activities. CPSS enables the management and control of physical objects, such as managing hospital care, helping students with their studies, assisting farmers in growing ripe fruit, helping drivers with vehicle repairs, and many others. In this paper, we highlight the main features of Cyber-Physical-Social Systems (CPSS), discuss its weaknesses, and identify its problems. In addition, we highlight the main attacks targeting the CPSS and the proposed security solutions. To further demonstrate the CPSS, we show its implementation in smart agriculture as a case study.

articleTitle: E-Bike Energy Needs Estimation based on Route Characteristics and Rider Behavior
publicationTitle: 2023 Eleventh International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Information Systems (ICICIS)
abstract: Environmental awareness triggered the popularity of electric bicycles (E-Bikes) which has seen a significant rise in recent years due to technological advancement. Nevertheless, some limitations affect this continuous growth notably Range Anxiety i.e., the fear of running out of energy mid-ride. While numerous studies have investigated energy prediction in electric vehicles, research on electric bikes remains relatively scarce. Hence, this paper proposes an energy prediction machine learning model that considers route characteristics and rider behavior based on data collected from different sensors mounted on the E-Bike. Different machine learning models were used: Multiple Linear Regression, Random Forest, Light Gradient Boosting Machine, and Extreme Gradient Boosting Machine, and then evaluated using multiple metrics such as Mean Squared Error, Mean Absolute Error, Latency, CPU Utilization, and R2 Score. According to the evaluation metrics, the random forest model outperformed in terms of its R2 score, Mean Squared Error, and Mean Absolute Error, achieving the highest accuracy and lowest errors. However, it exhibited the poorest performance in terms of latency and CPU utilization.

articleTitle: Early Detection of Retinitis Pigmentosa
publicationTitle: 2023 Eleventh International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Information Systems (ICICIS)
abstract: Retinitis pigmentosa (RP) is a debilitating inherited retinal disorder that affects a significant number of individuals worldwide. Existing diagnostic methods have limitations in detecting early-stage RP and they highlight the need for using additional imaging modalities. In this paper, a groundbreaking approach for RP diagnosis is proposed using three imaging modalities and a CNN-based classification model achieving 97.7% accuracy. The proposed model demonstrates superior performance compared to previous work as it achieves higher accuracy. A segmentation model was also proposed to segment pigment spots and provide doctors with effective monitoring of the disease. The proposed segmentation model outperforms previously used methods by achieving 99.61% accuracy and higher values in most of the performance metrics, including specificity, precision, and Area Under Curve (AUC). The Segmentation and classification models were integrated into a web application providing a user-friendly and intuitive tool for RP diagnosis and paving the way for more accessible and effective diagnostic tools. This innovative approach democratizes healthcare by making RP diagnosis affordable and accessible to more people and improving the speed of clinical decision-making.

articleTitle: Multi-Class Eye Disease Classification Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 Eleventh International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Information Systems (ICICIS)
abstract: Retinal fundus diseases affect a significant portion of the population and can lead to vision loss or blindness if left untreated. In this work, we developed a deep learning-based system for the multi-class classification of eye diseases using a large dataset of retinal images. The system can accurately detect and classify normal, diabetic retinopathy, glaucoma, and cataracts with an overall accuracy rate of 92%. Additionally, it provides users with detailed information on the symptoms and descriptions of the classified diseases and allows for easy image uploading and classification tracking. Our work aims to address the need for an accurate and accessible tool for identifying eye diseases, enabling earlier intervention, and improving patient outcomes. We also aim to advance the field of ophthalmology by demonstrating the potential of deep learning algorithms to enhance disease diagnosis and management.

articleTitle: A Proposed Model for Loan Approval Prediction Using Explainable Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2023 Eleventh International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Information Systems (ICICIS)
abstract: With the rapid growth in the banking sector due to the current inflation in Egypt, many people go to the bank for a loan. This paper proposes a model that explains the result of the loan approval of bank applicants using explainable artificial intelligence. this study uses the "Give Me Some Credit" dataset with more than 120k rows so the paper trains the model on earlier records of bank applicants who applied before for a bank loan. The paper aims to elucidate the significance of employing explainable artificial intelligence in the banking industry, with a particular focus on loan approval. it shows how it is beneficial to use XAI instead of using manual loan approval or even using normal algorithms to approve or decline bank loaners. The paper clarifies the machine learning algorithm's explanation, disregarding model accuracy in favor of focusing solely on explaining the model to bankers. This involves replacing the traditional machine learning algorithm as the decision maker with the banker, who can approve or deny loans using the model's explanation.

articleTitle: Social Bot Detection based on Language-independent Stylometric Analysis using dual-channel multi-dimensional CNN
publicationTitle: 2023 Eleventh International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Information Systems (ICICIS)
abstract: Nowadays, people use social media to interact with one another regularly. Social media platforms have received a great deal of criticism for their ability to democratize digital communication. Also, Social networks are often abused to bias public opinion and promote falsehoods. Unfortunately, there have been instances when misinformation attempts have been managed by bots, Social media accounts handled by computer scripts that seem to be real humans. Using user activity patterns, we propose an innovative approach for detecting social bots, which does not rely on communicative language. The efficacy of our approach is demonstrated through its application to two languages that have been extensively studied by many scholars in the past. To evaluate its performance, we employ the CLEF 2019 dataset, which consists of sub-datasets in both English and Spanish. This study employs a dual-channel multi-dimensional convolutional neural network (DCMDCNN) model for the identification of social bots. The model incorporates four stylometric features that primarily capture user interactions in a language-independent way. Our proposed model outperforms many of the techniques used in this goal, with the highest accuracy of 93.45%, 90.72%, and 92.34% for English, Spanish, and Aggregated versions respectively.

articleTitle: Predictive Maintenance by Machine Learning Methods
publicationTitle: 2023 Eleventh International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Information Systems (ICICIS)
abstract: Predictive maintenance techniques are designed to determine the state of equipment in action to help us know when we can intervene to perform maintenance on it. Predictive maintenance design applies artificial intelligence techniques such as machine learning to analyze data and monitor efficiency. In this paper, we predict the maintenance of any equipment before it stops to reduce unplanned equipment maintenance by means of machine learning algorithms. We adopted in our work the following supervised machine learning algorithms: Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, KNN, Decision Tree, Logistic Regression, Naïve Bayes, and XGBOOST. Simulations and results show that the Random Forest and XGBOOST have almost the same performance. The XGBOOST machine learning algorithm is preferred for bigger datasets compared to Random Forest and it works more effectively in the case of small datasets. Finally, the proposed predictive maintenance system is successful in identifying possible failure indicators and reducing some production stoppages as shown by our simulation results.

articleTitle: Investigating the Relation between Code Comments and Issue Resolution Time in Java Repositories
publicationTitle: 2023 Eleventh International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Information Systems (ICICIS)
abstract: Source code comments play a critical role in software development by facilitating issue resolution and reducing maintenance time and cost. However, the impact of code comments, particularly those aiding program comprehension, on expediting issue resolution remains insufficiently explored. This study investigates the impact of code comments on issue resolution time for issues related to pulling requests involving code maintenance. To this end, ten of the most popular Java repositories on GitHub were selected, and closed pull request-related issues were identified using a specific criterion. Comments were then extracted from classes modified by the pull requests, and a trained BERT model was utilized to classify them according to their usefulness. The percentage of comments relative to code size, the percentage of useful comments relative to all comments, and the average issue resolution time were computed and examined for correlations. The results indicate a negative correlation (-0.68) between the percentage of code comments in modified classes and the average issue resolution time. A stronger negative correlation (-0.73) was found between the percentage of useful code comments to all comments in modified classes and the average issue resolution time per class. These findings demonstrate that code with more comments, particularly useful ones, leads to faster issue resolution. This serves as a basis for further research into the impact of various fine-grained comment types on issue resolution time in different programming languages. Also, it can assist developers in writing more effective comments that accelerate bug-fixing and reduce software maintenance efforts.
